description: A keywordless declaration (`unusedThing = 42`, §50.8.5 — a `const`) that falls out of scope never read is NOT E-MU-001 and not an error: an unread binding is the S422 unused-binding LINT, the same for every binding form (`let`, `const`, keywordless). E-MU-001 is "Must-use: return value of `!` function not captured" (§34). The case keeps its S412-era directory name; what it pins is the S479 ruling.
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md-S479-3B ("⭐ RULED — S478 hand-off §3.A and §3.B, PA recs adopted (S479, 2026-11-18)", §3.B: "S422 stands; an unread keywordless binding is the same lint as every other binding form; the E-MU-001 reading is rejected") · ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S422 "CALL 3 — unused-binding is a LINT across all binding forms, hard error later if it proves out"
rationale: S422 Call 3: "Population: ALL binding forms (`let` · `const` · bare)" — "you cannot split on 'was the keyword written'"; "Severity: LINT now". A lint never rejects, so the program compiles. The lint itself has no §34 code yet (g-spec-unused-binding-lint-code-s479); when it lands this case gains its warning code in `codes`.
